table_title: List the world's 20 busiest airports by 2025 annual passenger traffic (passengers in millions) — with each airport's country, host city, passenger volume, and world region. Source universe is Wikipedia's 'List of busiest airports by passenger traffic' master article, 2025 statistics section (Airports Council International sourced).
db_analog: SELECT a.airport_name AS airport, a.country, a.city, a.passengers_millions_2025 AS passengers, a.region FROM airports a WHERE a.passenger_rank_2025 <= 20 ORDER BY a.passengers_millions_2025 DESC, a.airport_name ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of busiest airports by passenger traffic' master article + 20 per-airport Wikipedia articles, all accessed 2026-05-14. Universe = top-20 airports by 2025 annual passenger traffic per the master article's '2025 statistics' section (sourced from Airports Council International / ACI). temporal_sensitivity = high because passenger-traffic values are annual throughput metrics that shift year-over-year — the master article updates the most-recent-year section annually, so within 12-18 months the staged 2025 snapshot will be superseded by a 2026 snapshot. Snapshot-year choice (2025) follows the master's current section header. **Canonical-source rule from worlds_largest_container_ports_by_2024_teu (time-series master-wins inversion) applies uniformly**: for time-series throughput metrics (annual passenger traffic), the master article wins because ACI updates the figures annually while per-airport Wikipedia article infoboxes can lag (some per-airport articles like Hartsfield–Jackson cite 108.1 M from 2024 in body text while the 2025 infobox + master concur at 106.3 M; Shenzhen Bao'an body still cites 52.7 M from 2023 while master 2025 reports 66.5 M; this is the same stale-infobox pattern as ports). For non-time-series static attributes (Country, City), per-airport article wins (entity-detail role). Region is a curator-assigned closed-vocabulary categorical from a fixed country-to-region mapping (same 9-value vocabulary as ports: East Asia / Southeast Asia / South Asia / Middle East / Europe / North America / Latin America / Africa / Oceania), not directly sourced from per-airport articles. Istanbul Airport staged Region = Europe per master-article grouping (Istanbul Airport is located on the European side of the Bosphorus; the master article ranks Istanbul under European regional groupings). All 20 airports are operational as of source-access date 2026-05-14; no construction-status exclusions needed.
_extraction_notes: Top_k instance — single-cell-per-row attribute lookup over a top-20-by-2025-passenger-traffic fixed entity set. **SATURATES `top_k` at 5/5 — SIXTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR** (joining factual_lookup 6/5, multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5). **Transportation/Aviation NEW subdomain** — the Transportation family extends from 2 instances (Road Traffic via `countries_that_drive_on_the_left`, Logistics via `worlds_largest_container_ports_by_2024_teu`) to 3 instances with this Aviation NEW subdomain. Schema: 5 cols (Airport PK + Country categorical + City categorical + Passengers (millions) numeric + Region categorical). Sort: Passengers (millions) DESC primary (busiest-first), Airport ASC alphabetical secondary tiebreaker (no exact ties in staged 20). Country distribution: United States 5 (dominates global airport rankings — Atlanta, DFW, O'Hare, Denver, LAX), China 4 (Shanghai Pudong, Guangzhou Baiyun, Beijing Capital, Shenzhen Bao'an), plus singletons for UAE, Japan, UK, Turkey, India, South Korea, France, Singapore, Netherlands, Spain, Malaysia (13 distinct countries, more diverse than the ports instance's 10 because aviation hubs span more nations than container-shipping hubs). Region distribution: East Asia 6, North America 5, Europe 5 (including Istanbul per master grouping), Southeast Asia 2, South Asia 1, Middle East 1 (6 distinct regions, matching ports). Passenger range: 63.3 (Kuala Lumpur) to 106.3 (Atlanta) — 43 M span across the top-20. Bridges + dams + ports cycle lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Airport using Wikipedia common-form names per per-airport article title with diacritics preserved (Hartsfield–Jackson en-dash U+2013; Adolfo Suárez acute á + Madrid–Barajas en-dash; Shenzhen Bao'an ASCII apostrophe); (b) per-row data sourced from 2 articles each (master + per-airport), 21 URLs total; (c) **canonical-source rule INVERSION for time-series passenger-traffic metric documented at Stage-1 (same as ports — master wins because ACI updates annually while per-airport infoboxes lag)**; (d) source_defined claim type honestly reflects the top-20-by-2025-passenger-traffic universe; (e) Istanbul Airport staged Region = Europe per master-article grouping (located on European side of Bosphorus); flagged as open_question for the Middle East alternative reading. Entity class: `engineered-structures/airports` (NEW fine-class in the `engineered-structures` bucket — bucket extends from 3 to 4 instances after this Ready, joining bridges + buildings + dams + airports). Article-name choices: 3 master-vs-per-article name differences resolved in favor of per-airport article title (Wikipedia common-form rule): 'Haneda Airport' (master uses 'Tokyo Haneda Airport'); 'O'Hare International Airport' (master uses 'Chicago O'Hare International Airport'); 'Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport' (with slash per article URL, master uses space-separated 'Dallas Fort Worth'). 'Singapore Changi Airport' is a concurrence (both master and per-article use the same form).
